scope: English and Spanish New Jersey first-time home buyer due-diligence guides

methodology.principle: Use the public agency responsible for each step, avoid market forecasts and generalized dollar assumptions, and send readers back to current program, contract, property, loan, insurance, title, appraisal, and closing documents.
volatile_values_excluded: down-payment percentages and minimum credit scores
assistance award amounts and county income or purchase-price limits
closing-cost percentages and vendor price ranges
home-price forecasts and town affordability rankings

blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.html.publisher: New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency
blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.html.fact_supported: NJHMFA publishes the current first-mortgage and down-payment-assistance product pages, fact sheets, participating-lender path, and program-limit resources.

blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.html.publisher: New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency
blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.html.fact_supported: NJHMFA states that its FAQs are general information rather than final requirements and directs applicants to current program materials and participating lenders.

blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.html.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.html.fact_supported: HUD provides the official FHA homebuyer resource center and contact path for loan-program questions.

blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.html.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.html.fact_supported: HUD maintains the official search and telephone path for participating housing-counseling agencies.
CFPB recommends comparing written mortgage offers and identifies loan terms, payment structure, program type, costs, points, and other fields to evaluate.
CFPB explains how to compare Loan Estimates, including loan amount, rate, monthly payment, mortgage insurance, cash to close, origination charges, points, and credits.

blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.html.publisher: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance
blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.html.fact_supported: NJDOBI explains New Jersey brokerage relationships, written brokerage service agreements, required agreement terms, and the rule that broker compensation is negotiable and not set by law.

blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.html.publisher: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance
blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.html.fact_supported: The State consumer guide explains attorney review for licensee-prepared contracts, contract-controlled deadlines, independent inspection, title review, insurance, and settlement preparation.
CFPB organizes underwriting, inspection, insurance, title, document review, closing, and post-closing checkpoints for covered mortgage transactions.
CFPB defines an appraisal as an independent opinion of value and explains the borrower's right to a copy for a typical covered home loan.
CFPB distinguishes lender and owner's title insurance and explains that consumers can generally shop for title providers.

blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.html.publisher: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance
blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.html.fact_supported: NJDOBI publishes model policy summaries to help consumers review homeowners and condominium coverage and exclusions.
CFPB provides the official Closing Disclosure explainer and directs borrowers to compare final loan terms and costs before closing.
The State provides official property-tax and assessment information; a buyer must confirm the current record for the specific parcel and municipality.

es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.publisher: New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency
es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.fact_supported: NJHMFA publica las páginas vigentes de hipotecas, asistencia, hojas informativas, prestamistas participantes y límites de los programas.

es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.publisher: New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency
es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.fact_supported: NJHMFA aclara que sus preguntas frecuentes son información general y remite a los materiales vigentes y a prestamistas participantes para los requisitos finales.

es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.fact_supported: HUD mantiene el recurso oficial de FHA y el canal de contacto para preguntas sobre préstamos asegurados por FHA.

es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.fact_supported: HUD mantiene la búsqueda oficial y el teléfono para encontrar agencias participantes de asesoría de vivienda.

es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.publisher: Oficina para la Protección Financiera del Consumidor
es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.fact_supported: La CFPB explica en español la Estimación del Préstamo, la Divulgación del Cierre y las excepciones de ciertos productos hipotecarios.

es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.publisher: Oficina para la Protección Financiera del Consumidor
es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.fact_supported: La CFPB indica cómo comparar una Estimación del Préstamo revisada y qué preguntas hacer sobre cambios en el préstamo y el efectivo para el cierre.

es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.publisher: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance
es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.fact_supported: NJDOBI explica las relaciones de corretaje, los acuerdos escritos, sus términos obligatorios y que la compensación del corredor es negociable y no está fijada por ley.

es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.publisher: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance
es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.fact_supported: La guía estatal explica la revisión por abogado de contratos preparados por licenciatarios, los plazos del contrato, la inspección independiente, el título, el seguro y el cierre.
La CFPB organiza las verificaciones de suscripción, inspección, seguro, título, documentos y cierre para hipotecas cubiertas.
La CFPB define la tasación como una opinión independiente de valor y explica el derecho a recibir una copia en un préstamo típico cubierto.
La CFPB distingue el seguro de título del prestamista del seguro de título del propietario y explica la posibilidad general de comparar proveedores.

es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.publisher: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance
es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.fact_supported: NJDOBI publica resúmenes modelo para revisar coberturas y exclusiones de pólizas de vivienda y condominio.

es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.publisher: Oficina para la Protección Financiera del Consumidor
es/blog/first-time-home-buyer-nj-guide.h.fact_supported: La CFPB recomienda preguntar por cargos y tasas, comparar opciones antes del cierre y resolver diferencias con el prestamista o agente de cierre.
El Estado publica información oficial sobre impuestos y tasaciones; el comprador debe verificar el registro vigente de la parcela y el municipio específicos.
